doc.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]

title: Bill Challis's 75th birthday photos and the Whiteman band picture
summary: Budd shows a photo and program, and names those in a picture of Whiteman-era musicians.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Oh you’ll hear the same. There’s so many things. You know Bill Challis. I made a friend. I wanted to see him, when he died. This is Bill Challis‘ 75th birthday. That’s not on the machine? We’re off it?
No we’re still going, that’s okay.
Oh I don’t want to talk about this. You can erase stuff?

This is something entirely different. I always wanted to meet Bill Challis who wrote the orchestration for the Goldkettes and later for Paul Whiteman. And he had his 75th birthday party and here’s a picture. A handsome guy when he was young.

That’s when he was with the Paul Whiteman band, and he had his 75th birthday and that’s the party he had, and this is the program. And Bill Jones you may know, played the piano, and I know Challis went to Bucknell University and this is the speech he made there too, it’s remarkable. I wouldn’t want to lose that, but...
I wonder if Spiegle Wilcox is in this picture.

Yes he is. I know all those guys in that. That’s Spiegle Wilcox right there. That’s the Doc, they call him Doc Riker. He’s the saxophone player. This is Beiderbecke right there, that’s the trombone player, that’s Bill Challis, that is probably Chauncey Morehouse, that’s Steve Brown the bass player. I don’t know who that is, this is Frank Trumbauer, no that’s the long tell guitar player, I forget his name, I shouldn’t forget it but I’ve forgotten those names. This is Itsy Riskin who is one of the piano players. And somebody from that same — oh Mr. Challis, he died before I got to see him but his brother is still alive, stroked but still living, and he sent me — no that’s another that’s not it — another thing, Evan Challis, he sent me a picture of this, Paul Mertz, who played, and Evan Challis sent me this note, and I’ve never seen him except with our writing we’ve become friends. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -19-
